CHAPTER 2.3 · LEARNING AREA 2

CHAPTER 2.3 · LEARNING AREA 2 · JANUARY

Composite solids

A water tower, a grain silo, a workpiece with a drilled hole: most solids in everyday life are put together from prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres. You learn to split them into known parts or to complete them to a known solid, and in this way to calculate volume, surface area and the material needed.

4 LESSONS1 UNIT2 LABS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • split composite solids into known solids or complete them to a solid
  • calculate their volume and their mass
  • calculate their surface area and decide which faces lie on the outside
  • find the material needed in word problems
CHECK-IN: CAN YOU ALREADY DO THIS?

Cylinder with $r = 2$ cm and $h = 5$ cm. Volume? Round to two decimal places.

$20\pi \approx 62.83\,\text{cm}^3$

Pyramid with $G = 16\,\text{cm}^2$ and $h = 3$ cm. Volume?

$\tfrac13 \cdot 16 \cdot 3 = 16\,\text{cm}^3$

Cone with $r = 3$ m and $h = 4$ m. How long is the slant height?

$\sqrt{9 + 16} = 5$ m

A hemisphere has $r = 3$ cm. Its volume is $\square \cdot \pi$. Which number belongs in the box?

$\tfrac12 \cdot \tfrac43 \pi \cdot 27 = 18\pi$

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Splitting and completing

A tower consists of a cylinder ($r = 3$ m, $h = 8$ m) and a conical roof with a height of 4 m. Its volume is the sum of the parts: $V = \pi \cdot 9 \cdot 8 + \tfrac13 \cdot \pi \cdot 9 \cdot 4 = 72\pi + 12\pi = 84\pi \approx 264\,\text{m}^3$. For the surface area the face between the cylinder and the roof does not count: it lies inside.

KEY POINT · COMPOSITE SOLIDS

Splitting: divide the solid into known solids and add their volumes.

Completing: complete it to a known solid and subtract what is too much, for example a drilled hole.

Surface area: only the faces on the outside count. Faces where two parts touch disappear, the inner wall of a drilled hole is added.

First sketch and name the parts, then calculate each part separately.

The formulas: cylinder $\pi r^2 h$ · cone $\tfrac13 \pi r^2 h$ · sphere $\tfrac43 \pi r^3$ · pyramid $\tfrac13 G h$ · prism $G h$.

Hemisphere: volume $\tfrac23 \pi r^3$, curved surface $2\pi r^2$.

INTERACTIVE · TOWER AND SILO

Choose the tower or the silo and change the measurements. For the volume the parts are added, for the surface area the face between them is missing.

EXAMPLE 1 · THE SILO

A silo is a cylinder with $r = 2$ m and $h = 8$ m, with a hemisphere on top. How much does it hold? How large is its outer surface including the floor?

$V = \pi \cdot 4 \cdot 8 + \tfrac23 \pi \cdot 8 = 32\pi + \tfrac{16}{3}\pi \approx 117.3\,\text{m}^3$.

Outside: floor $4\pi$, curved surface of the cylinder $32\pi$, hemisphere $8\pi$, together $44\pi \approx 138.2\,\text{m}^2$.

EXAMPLE 2 · THE WORKPIECE

A steel cube with an edge length of 6 cm has a hole with a diameter of 2 cm drilled right through its middle. Calculate the volume, the mass ($\varrho = 7.85\,\tfrac{\text{g}}{\text{cm}^3}$) and the surface area.

Completing: $V = 216 - \pi \cdot 1^2 \cdot 6 \approx 197.2\,\text{cm}^3$, $m \approx 7.85 \cdot 197.2 \approx 1548$ g.

Surface area: $216 - 2\pi + 2\pi \cdot 1 \cdot 6 \approx 247.4\,\text{cm}^2$. Two circles are missing, the inner wall is added.

EXERCISES

An advertising column is a cylinder with $r = 0.7$ m and $h = 3$ m with a conical roof 0.6 m high. Calculate its volume.

$V = \pi \cdot 0.49 \cdot 3 + \tfrac13 \cdot \pi \cdot 0.49 \cdot 0.6 = 1.47\pi + 0.098\pi \approx 4.93\,\text{m}^3$

An ice-cream cone (cone, $r = 3$ cm, $h = 10$ cm) is filled to the brim, with half a scoop of ice cream with $r = 3$ cm on top. How much ice cream is it?

$30\pi + 18\pi = 48\pi \approx 150.8\,\text{cm}^3$

A concrete pipe is 1 m long, it has a radius of 5 cm on the outside and 4 cm on the inside. How much concrete is in it? How heavy is it ($\varrho = 2.4\,\tfrac{\text{g}}{\text{cm}^3}$)?

$V = \pi \cdot (25 - 16) \cdot 100 = 900\pi \approx 2827\,\text{cm}^3$, $m \approx 6786$ g, that is about 6.8 kg.

A garden pavilion is a cube with an edge length of 4 m with a pyramid roof 3 m high. Calculate the volume and the outer surface without the floor.

$V = 64 + \tfrac13 \cdot 16 \cdot 3 = 80\,\text{m}^3$. $h_s = \sqrt{9 + 4} \approx 3.61$ m, roof $2 \cdot 4 \cdot 3.61 \approx 28.8\,\text{m}^2$, walls $64\,\text{m}^2$, together about $92.8\,\text{m}^2$.

A flower pot has the shape of a frustum of a cone. If you complete it downwards, you get a cone with $r = 6$ cm and $h = 12$ cm. A small cone with $r = 3$ cm and $h = 6$ cm has been cut off. How much soil fits into it?

$V = \tfrac13 \pi \cdot 36 \cdot 12 - \tfrac13 \pi \cdot 9 \cdot 6 = 144\pi - 18\pi = 126\pi \approx 395.8\,\text{cm}^3$

TEST YOURSELF!

A tower consists of a cylinder with 90 m³ and a conical roof with 30 m³. What is its volume?

$90 + 30 = 120\,\text{m}^3$

A cube with 1000 cm³ has a drilled hole with 100 cm³. How large is the remaining volume?

$1000 - 100 = 900\,\text{cm}^3$

The outer surface of the silo from example 1 is $\square \cdot \pi$. Which number belongs in the box?

$4 + 32 + 8 = 44$

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

A house is a cuboid (10 m long, 8 m wide, 6 m high) with a gable roof. The gable is 8 m wide and 3 m high. How large is the enclosed space?

$480 + \tfrac12 \cdot 8 \cdot 3 \cdot 10 = 480 + 120 = 600\,\text{m}^3$

Connecting with chapter 2.2: the largest possible sphere is turned from a wooden cube with an edge length of 10 cm. What percentage of the wood becomes shavings?

Sphere: $\tfrac43 \pi \cdot 125 \approx 523.6\,\text{cm}^3$. Shavings: $1000 - 523.6 = 476.4\,\text{cm}^3$, that is about 47.6%.

A capsule consists of a cylinder ($r = 0.5$ cm, $h = 1.5$ cm) with a hemisphere at each end. Calculate its volume.

Cylinder $0.375\pi$, two hemispheres make a whole sphere: $\tfrac43 \pi \cdot 0.125 \approx 0.167\pi$. Together $\approx 0.542\pi \approx 1.70\,\text{cm}^3$.

A water tower is a cylinder with $r = 4$ m with a hemisphere on top. The tank is to hold 500 m³. How high must the cylinder be?

Hemisphere: $\tfrac23 \pi \cdot 64 \approx 134.0\,\text{m}^3$. That leaves $366.0\,\text{m}^3$ for the cylinder: $h = \tfrac{366.0}{16\pi} \approx 7.28$ m.

EXCURSIONBUILDINGS

The sphere of the Berlin TV tower

The TV tower at Alexanderplatz in Berlin was built from 1965 to 1969. At 368 m it is the tallest structure in Germany. It is a composite solid: a slender concrete shaft, on top of it a sphere with a diameter of 32 m, above that the antenna.

Inside the sphere there are a viewing floor and a restaurant that slowly turns around. From there you can see far beyond Berlin in clear weather.

Work it out: what are the volume and the surface area of the sphere?

$r = 16$ m: $V = \tfrac43 \pi \cdot 4096 \approx 17\,157\,\text{m}^3$, $O = 4\pi \cdot 256 \approx 3217\,\text{m}^2$. That is almost half a football pitch.

Source: Berlin TV Tower, information from the operator (built 1965–1969, height 368 m, diameter of the sphere 32 m).

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

SPLITTING

divide into known solids, add the volumes

Tower: $72\pi + 12\pi = 84\pi$

COMPLETING

complete to a known solid, subtract what is too much

Cube with a hole: $216 - 6\pi$

SURFACE AREA

only outer faces, touching faces disappear, drilled holes add inner walls

Silo: $4\pi + 32\pi + 8\pi$

MASS

$m = \varrho \cdot V$

197 cm³ of steel: about 1.5 kg

TESTTWO ROUNDS · INSTANT FEEDBACK
ROUND 1 · IN YOUR HEAD

Cube with 64 m³ and pyramid roof with 16 m³. Total volume?

80 m³

A cylinder with a base of 10 cm² stands on a cuboid. By how much is the outer surface smaller than both surface areas together?

The base of the cylinder and the equally large piece of the top face lie inside: $2 \cdot 10 = 20\,\text{cm}^2$.

A cuboid has a drilled hole. What is the easiest way to calculate its volume?

Cuboid without the hole minus the hole.

$84\pi \approx 263.89\,\text{m}^3$

Ice-cream cone ($r = 3$ cm, $h = 10$ cm) with half a scoop ($r = 3$ cm). Volume? Round to two decimal places.

$48\pi \approx 150.80\,\text{cm}^3$

Cube with a 6 cm edge, a hole with a diameter of 2 cm drilled right through. Remaining volume? Round to two decimal places.

$216 - 6\pi \approx 197.15\,\text{cm}^3$
